title: The best waterfront hotel in America is in Massachusetts, according to USA Today readers
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Chatham Bars Inn in Chatham, Cape Cod, was named the best waterfront hotel in the U.S. by USA Today readers.
Another New England hotel, Madison Beach Hotel in Madison, Connecticut, secured the fourth spot on USA Today's list.
USA Today's 2026 10Best Readers' Choice Awards ranks top waterfront hotels through reader votes among expert-selected nominees.

title: Are millionaires really leaving Massachusetts? We don’t know yet.
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: IRS migration data for post-2023 millionaires tax isn't available, fueling debate over wealthy residents leaving Massachusetts.
Census data shows Massachusetts had a net domestic outflow of over 30,000 from July 2024 to July 2025.
Massachusetts saw a 36% increase in millionaires from 2018 to 2022, less than Montana's 132% and Florida's 77%.

title: 7 things to do during a rainy day on the Cape
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Chatham Shark Center offers interactive exhibits and activities like the Fossil Pit Experience for learning about sharks.
Indoor Fins Up! Waterpark in Hyannis provides slides and a lazy river with day passes available for non-guests.
Explore Cape Cod's museums and historic homes, including the John F. Kennedy Hyannis Museum and Hoxie House in Sandwich.

title: Visit to Boston made Boca Raton resident feel miserable about living in Boca Raton
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Ian Pinto's Boston visit prompted reflection on Boca Raton's lifestyle after experiencing Boston's walkability and public transit.
The trip highlighted differences in cost, with Pinto finding Boston surprisingly affordable compared to Boca Raton.
Pinto praised Boston's inclusive environment and hopes to move there, inspired to explore beyond his hometown.

title: Motorcyclist killed in crash with pickup truck in Raynham
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Jason Marshall, 31, from Taunton, was killed in a motorcycle crash with a pickup truck in Raynham.
Accident occurred at the intersection of Route 138 and Elm Street shortly before 8 p.m. Tuesday.
The pickup truck driver remained at the scene; investigation by State Police and Raynham police is ongoing.

title: N.H. police seek to identify suspects who fatally shot dog in attempted armed robbery
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A dog was fatally shot during an attempted armed robbery in Hollis, New Hampshire, early Tuesday morning.
The Hollis Police Department is investigating after a man and woman allegedly demanded money at gunpoint.
Authorities ask residents with security footage from the area between 2 a.m. and 4 a.m. to contact police.

title: Former Red Sox infielder criticized front office: ‘Some people watch the game, some people go on the computer’
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Vaughn Grissom criticized the Red Sox for an analytics-heavy approach, feeling undervalued during his tenure from 2023 to 2025.
Grissom, now with the Angels, claims his playing abilities were affected more by organizational trust than personal changes.
The Red Sox have faced previous critiques over their reliance on data, linked to chief baseball officer Craig Breslow.

title: Authorities investigating 4 family members shot in N.H. as potential attempted murders and suicide
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A 29-year-old man died by suicide and three family members were hospitalized following a shooting in Whitefield, NH.
Eric Blake Sr., among the injured, drove himself to the hospital with a gunshot wound and is stable.
The incident is being investigated as potential attempted murders and suicide with no threat to the public, officials say.

title: Lindsay Clancy sobs in court as medical examiner testifies about children’s autopsies
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Judge William Sullivan paused the trial after Lindsay Clancy broke down during Dr. Barbara Olson's testimony on her children's autopsies.
Medical examiner Dr. Barbara Olson testified that 5-year-old Cora and 3-year-old Dawson Clancy died from asphyxia caused by ligature strangulation.
Neuropathologist Dr. Renee Stonebridge confirmed the Clancy children had injuries consistent with oxygen deprivation, indicating asphyxia.

title: Acton teen charged with murder used ChatGPT for ‘fantasies’ about killing family, DA says
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Arjun Aravind, 17, was charged with murdering his mother and brother in their Acton home, sparking an overnight manhunt.
Aravind allegedly used ChatGPT for creating stories about killing his family prior to the incident, according to officials.
He was arrested in Wayland early Wednesday and faces multiple charges, including murder, in Concord District Court.
